changes.before: If label receives Waiting instead, what prints?
changes.after: Use sealed types so Kotlin can check that a when expression handles every case.

before: A sealed interface restricts its direct implementations to permitted declarations in the same package and module. It lets a when expression cover the known direct alternatives rather than relying on a catch-all branch.

data object declares a singleton alternative with data-style operations. A data class carries information for another case. In the is Ready branch, the smart cast exposes text; Waiting has only one named instance.

Complete local Kotlin/JVM example; the app itself does not execute it:
```kotlin
sealed interface State
 data object Waiting : State
 data class Ready(val text: String) : State
fun label(state: State): String = when (state) {
    Waiting -> "waiting"
    is Ready -> state.text
}
fun main() { println(label(Ready("done"))) }
```
Expected output or behavior: done. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Add another direct case and update the when expression rather than hiding it with else. You may trace it without a Kotlin compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A sealed interface has a controlled set of direct implementations. They must be declared in the same package, a named code group, and module, a group of files built together. The compiler can then check which cases a when expression must handle.

This State has two cases. `data object Waiting` declares one named object with no changing input. `data class Ready` creates objects that carry text. In the Ready branch, the type check lets Kotlin read that text.

Follow the example one line at a time.
```kotlin
sealed interface State
 data object Waiting : State
 data class Ready(val text: String) : State
fun label(state: State): String = when (state) {
    Waiting -> "waiting"
    is Ready -> state.text
}
fun main() { println(label(Ready("done"))) }
```
The screen shows `done`. The value is a Ready object, so its text supplies the result.
A when that handles every possible case is called exhaustive. This one needs no else branch. Adding a new direct case means this when must also handle it.

before.question: If label receives Waiting instead, what prints?
choices: A compile error because Waiting has no text.
before.explanation: The singleton case chooses its own branch and never attempts to read Ready.text.

after.question: Pass Waiting to label instead. What appears?
choices: A compile error because Waiting has no text.
after.explanation: Waiting selects its own branch, which returns waiting. That branch never reads Ready.text.
